statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. The Sunday restart has now held the same 29,535.25-29,594.25 band for a third hour while volume roughly doubled to about 9.0k contracts, so depth is building without any range extension and the weekend gap risk from the US-Iran tanker exchange has resolved without an adverse repricing. Tail returns to the low-band floor. Stress stays elevated on a war-premium energy complex, a restrictive Treasury curve and a holiday-thinned Monday session that halts early.
recommendation: Conditions map to EA_ON for NQ futures and NAS100 CFD. Conditional risk is concentrated in the narrow 15:00-17:00 UTC window into the early Labor Day futures halt and, later, in the 22:00 UTC restart for the Tuesday trade date, rather than across the whole outlook; every forecast hour maps below the block threshold. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this mapping.
headline: Nasdaq-100 futures have held a 59-point restart band into a third hour while the weekend US-Iran tanker exchange left Brent up less than one percent
body:
The Sunday restart is roughly two and a half hours old and the observed price path has still not extended. NQ front-month last printed between 29,565.25 and 29,571.25 inside an unchanged 29,535.25-29,594.25 session range, and volume has roughly doubled to about 9.0k contracts since the previous assessment. Volume building while the range does not is the signature of orderly two-way price discovery rather than directional efficiency, and two independent quote sources agree on the level. Against Friday's Nasdaq-100 cash close of 29,544.15 the restart is effectively flat, so the adverse weekend gap that the closed-venue hours had to carry did not materialise.

The weekend produced a genuine escalation in the Iran conflict. US Central Command struck three Iranian oil tankers on 5 September after the Revolutionary Guard fired ballistic missiles at a US carrier and destroyer, and Iran in turn targeted tankers it said were using unauthorised routes. The market response has been notably contained: Brent trades near $96.5 and WTI near $91.9, each up under one percent, and both were already war-elevated from roughly $70 before the Strait of Hormuz was effectively closed in February. OPEC+ separately left October output quotas unchanged, an outcome that landed as expected. This reads as a chronic, largely priced conflict rather than a fresh discontinuity, which is why the escalation supports Stress and not Tail.

Cross-asset alignment is absent. Friday's VIX close of 14.53 is low in absolute terms, the H.15 curve is restrictive but stable with the two-year at 4.34% and the ten-year at 4.77%, and the delayed cross-asset context shows index, rate, gold and volatility futures all within a few basis points of unchanged. Friday's Nasdaq internals were split rather than aligned, with semiconductors sharply higher and most megacaps lower, which is a rotational tape rather than one-way index structure. No shallow-pullback pattern, failed retracement or extreme holding has been observed, so Tail sits at the low-band floor.

Monday is Labor Day. US cash equity markets are closed and CME equity index futures halt early at 17:00 UTC, leaving a thin session with no domestic cash depth. Conditional Tail therefore lifts modestly around the European open, where the weekend headlines first meet real depth, and peaks in the final hour before the halt, where squaring into an early close meets the thinnest book of the day. It returns to the closed-venue floor across the five shut hours and lifts again at the 22:00 UTC restart for the Tuesday trade date. Every hour of the outlook remains inside the low band.

lookbackSummary: Twenty-three of the 24 preceding hourly Claude assessments are available; the 21:00 UTC hour has no published assessment and is marked unavailable with null fields. Across the closed-venue Sunday hours Tail held a flat 5, with a single 4 at 02:00 UTC, mapping to EA_ON and green throughout, before stepping to 8 at the 22:00 UTC restart hour to carry reopen-gap risk and easing to 6 once the restart proved orderly. Stress climbed from 54 through a 52-58 band to a 60 high at 20:00 UTC as Sunday's geopolitical flow accumulated, then eased to 57 and 56 after the reopen. Confidence stayed in an 84-86 band and dominant mode was normal for every available hour.
outlookSummary: The next 24 hours cover the remainder of the Sunday restart, a full Asian session, a European session traded against a closed US market on Labor Day, a shortened futures session that halts at 17:00 UTC, five closed hours and the 22:00 UTC restart for the Tuesday trade date. Conditional Tail stays inside the low band for every hour: 5 through the Asian session now that the reopen has proved contained, 7 around the European open where the weekend Iran headlines first meet real depth without a US cash backstop, 6 to 7 across the holiday-thinned afternoon, a peak of 9 in the final hour before the early halt, the closed-venue floor of 5 while futures are shut, and 8 at the Tuesday restart. Stress holds in a 54-58 elevated band and confidence decays from 86 to 74 with forecast distance. The danger window is deliberately narrow at 15:00-17:00 UTC, covering the European cash close into the early Labor Day futures halt.

forecast.analysis: Third hour of the Sunday restart: NQ last printed 29,565-29,571 inside an unchanged 29,535.25-29,594.25 band while volume roughly doubled to about 9.0k. Depth is building without range extension, Tokyo opens into a flat tape, and the weekend Iran escalation has not repriced equities, so Tail sits at the low-band floor.
drivers: NQ 59-point restart band unchanged for a third hour as volume rose to ~9.0k
Restart effectively flat against Friday's 29,544.15 Nasdaq-100 cash close
Tokyo cash open lands into an already orderly, two-way futures tape
Brent ~$96.5 up under 1% despite the weekend US-Iran tanker exchange

forecast.analysis: Hong Kong and mainland cash open inside this hour. The conditional risk is that an Asian venue reprices the weekend tanker exchange that Globex has so far ignored; the working assumption is continued two-way trade, with a decisive break of the 29,535/29,594 restart band as the invalidation to watch.

Restart band 29,535.25-29,594.25 is the conditional invalidation reference
Asian venues are the first depth able to reprice the weekend escalation

forecast.analysis: Mid-Asian session with no scheduled US data. Conditional Tail stays at the low-band floor because the observed restart produced no directional efficiency to extend from. Friday's split Nasdaq internals, with semis strongly higher against mostly lower megacaps, argue against one-way index structure forming here.
drivers: No scheduled US macro release falls inside this hour
Friday internals split: semis strongly higher, megacaps mostly lower
Assumes Asian trade absorbs rather than extends Iran headline flow

forecast.analysis: Asian afternoon. Energy is the transmission channel worth checking: Brent near $96.5 and WTI near $91.9 already carry a war premium, so a further oil impulse would have to be large to move index risk. Absent that, conditional Tail holds at the floor and the tape is assumed to stay range-bound.
drivers: Brent ~$96.5 and WTI ~$91.9 already carry a substantial war premium
Oil is the main transmission channel from Hormuz into index risk
Checkpoint: an outsized energy impulse, not a headline on its own

news.title: Opec+ keeps oil output policy unchanged for October amid Iran war uncertainty

forecast.analysis: Late Asian hours ahead of the European handover. Liquidity thins between the Tokyo close and the first European pre-market bids, so any repricing here would be conditional and low-depth rather than structural. Scores are unchanged at the low-band floor.
drivers: Liquidity thins between the Asian close and European pre-market
Low-depth moves here are not treated as evidence of persistent structure
US Labor Day removes the usual cash-session backstop later today

forecast.analysis: Pre-European hour. The observed evidence base is still the flat, contained restart and no new scheduled catalyst falls here. Conditional Tail remains at the floor; the checkpoint is whether European pre-market quotes open near the restart band rather than away from it.
drivers: No scheduled catalyst inside this hour
Checkpoint: European pre-market quotes relative to the restart band
Assessment still rests on the observed flat, contained Globex restart

forecast.analysis: Tokyo cash closes at 06:00 UTC and European pre-positioning begins. Conditional Tail lifts a point for the liquidity transition, because handovers are where an unabsorbed weekend headline typically surfaces. This is a checkpoint rather than an observation, and orderly two-way trade remains the base case.
drivers: Tokyo cash close at 06:00 UTC starts the first liquidity handover
Handover hours are where unabsorbed weekend headlines usually surface
The lift to Tail 6 is conditional, not based on observed structure

forecast.analysis: European cash opens. This is the first venue with real depth able to reprice the weekend US-Iran tanker exchange, and with US cash shut for Labor Day there is no later domestic session to absorb it. Conditional Tail lifts to 7 on that asymmetry; a contained European open would return it toward the floor.
drivers: European cash open is the first deep venue since the weekend escalation
US cash closed for Labor Day removes the later absorption session
Invalidation: a contained European open returns Tail toward the floor

news.title: US, Iran engaged in tanker war: Where is the months-long conflict headed?

forecast.analysis: London is fully open and European volumes peak for the day. Conditional risk concentrates in energy-linked and semiconductor names given Brent near $96.5 and Friday's strong chip tape. Rotational rather than directional trade is assumed; repeated extension after failed pullbacks would be the signal that changes it.

Energy-linked and semiconductor names carry the conditional beta

Stress stays elevated on the war-premium energy complex and a restrictive but stable curve, with the two-year at 4.34% against a 4.77% ten-year.

forecast.analysis: European late morning. With US venues shut, index futures track European cash and the oil complex rather than domestic flow. Conditional Tail holds at 6; the checkpoint is whether Brent stays near $96.5 or breaks out, since energy is the only cross-asset channel currently carrying the Iran conflict into equities.
drivers: Index futures track European cash and oil while US venues are shut
Checkpoint: Brent holding near $96.5 versus a decisive breakout

forecast.analysis: Final European morning hour. No scheduled release lands here, and Tuesday's NFIB survey and New York Fed consumer inflation expectations are the next calendar checkpoints. Conditional Tail is unchanged, with range trade on holiday-thinned volume the assumed regime.

No scheduled release falls inside this hour

forecast.analysis: The hour that would normally carry the US cash open is empty because of Labor Day. That removes the single most common source of opening-auction continuation, which is why conditional Tail stays in the low band rather than lifting the way a normal Monday open would justify.
drivers: No US cash open: Labor Day closes NYSE and Nasdaq for the session
Opening-auction continuation risk is absent from this hour
Futures depth is the only price discovery available

forecast.analysis: Early US-holiday afternoon. Depth falls away with domestic desks out, so a headline landing here would meet the thinnest absorption of the European overlap. Conditional Tail lifts a point on liquidity alone; no directional structure has been observed that would justify more.
drivers: US desks largely absent, cutting the tape's absorption capacity
The Tail lift reflects liquidity, not observed directional structure
Active Iran headline flow is the plausible trigger for a thin-tape move

forecast.analysis: The holiday afternoon continues with European cash heading into its final ninety minutes. The conditional risk is a low-depth extension that reverses once Europe closes. That pattern is scored as Stress rather than Tail unless retracements begin failing repeatedly.
drivers: European cash enters its final ninety minutes of trade
A low-depth extension that reverses is scored as Stress, not Tail
Repeatedly failing retracements would be the escalation trigger

forecast.analysis: European cash closes at 15:30 UTC and the danger window opens. Once Europe is out, holiday futures carry the tape alone into an early halt and depth is at its thinnest. Conditional Tail lifts to 8 for that structural reason; the window is deliberately narrow and every hour maps below the block threshold.
drivers: European cash close at 15:30 UTC removes the last deep venue
Danger window opens: 15:00-17:00 UTC on thin holiday depth
Every forecast hour still maps below the block threshold

forecast.analysis: Final hour before CME equity index futures halt at 17:00 UTC for Labor Day. Squaring into an early close on already thin depth is the least forgiving pocket of the outlook, so conditional Tail peaks at 9. It stays inside the low band, and the peak is a liquidity judgement rather than observed structure.
drivers: CME equity index futures halt at 17:00 UTC for Labor Day
Squaring into an early close on thin depth is the least forgiving pocket
Peak Tail 9 is a liquidity judgement, not observed one-way structure

forecast.analysis: Venue closed. With no price discovery available for five hours, conditional Tail returns to the closed-venue floor of 5. The only accumulating exposure is headline risk, which would express itself at the 22:00 UTC restart rather than inside this hour.

forecast.analysis: Third closed hour. Confidence drifts lower purely with forecast distance rather than because evidence has degraded, since no observation can be made while the venue is shut. Conditional Tail is unchanged at the closed-venue floor.

Confidence drift reflects forecast distance, not degraded evidence

forecast.analysis: Globex reopens for the Tuesday trade date after five closed hours. Conditional Tail lifts to 8 to carry reopen-gap risk, matching the level assigned to Sunday's restart before it proved contained. Nothing about Tuesday's path is observed; this is a scheduled structural checkpoint.

forecast.analysis: First full hour after the Tuesday restart. If the reopen behaves as Sunday's did, holding a narrow band while volume builds, conditional Tail eases back toward the floor. A gap that keeps extending on shallow pullbacks would be the evidence arguing the other way.
drivers: First full hour of the Tuesday restart on thin early Asian depth
Easing assumes a narrow band holding while volume builds
